A test holds every listed line: the entry exists and is a data entry; its file hashes to the listed hash; each listed key is one of the entry's seals and every seal is listed; and each listed hash is what an isolated run mints, except a line marked expect=refused, which the test holds to differ in exactly one listed seal hash. THE SHIP PATH: sh tools/deploy.sh --mint <name>, --mint-check <name> and --mint-retract <name> (each repeatable) are handed, by new lines in deploy.sh placed beside the --build lines after the lines that name the box, to tools/mint_ship.sh with the box in its environment, so no new file names the box; deploy.sh without them runs exactly as before. mint_ship.sh takes listed names only, never a path or a free argument, refuses DEPLOY_NO_GATE, and before any call checks that the name is listed once, its line is well formed, and the laptop's data/sticks/<name>.json hashes to the listed hash. It calls ssh and scp and nothing else that reaches the box, and never runs verify_deploy.py or any child with box settings of its own.

THE UNIT, tools/stick_mint.py mint|retract <name> --root <root> --run-id <id>, runs on the box under data/mints/.lock, a lock held only by mints that the kernel drops if the process dies (a second mint is refused and writes its refusal only to its own run id's result). It refuses to start unless available memory is at least its cap plus 256 MB, records the reading, and runs itself at oom_score_adj 1000 under nice and ionice, so if memory runs short the kernel ends the mint, never an engine; the step measures the unit's peak resident memory minting the canary entries in a temporary root and sets the cap, at most 1024 MB, as the address-space limit where the platform supports it and the test shows it holds there. Its environment holds no CONCORDANCE_ variable from its parent; it sets CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR to <root>/data, the keeping deploy/nh-engine.service names, CONCORDANCE_SEAL_INDEX=0 (tools/tick.py's cold seal path: the CAS object, the ledger link and the receipt and verified card copies are written, the live corpus is not touched, src/concordance/receipts.py:55-64), WEB_FIND_DISABLED=1, and src/ of <root> on its import path; and it refuses if <root>/.env names any keeping location (the five names above), reading the names only. It never restarts an engine: GET /sticks and GET /stick fold data/sticks.jsonl on each request (src/concordance/tickstick.py listing and read), and the cards join at the next corpus load, as they always have for tick.py.

THE ORDER, fail-closed, writing nothing before step 3: (1) load the catalog from <root>/data/sticks with concordance.sticks.load_catalog, take the entry, and refuse unless it is a data entry whose file hashes to the listed hash. (2) DRY RUN: verify every seal through verify_derivation as concordance.sticks.seal does, and compute each record's content hash with the CAS's own function (cas.content_hash_of over receipts.record_from_derivation(...).to_dict()), writing nothing; refuse unless every seal HOLDS and every hash equals its listed hash; then compute, with the same predicate as concordance.sticks.mint_marks, which seals are not yet in the CAS and which marks are not yet kept, and for a line marked expect=present refuse if any seal or mark would be added. (3) MINT: concordance.sticks.run(entry), the same seal path and mint loop tools/tick.py uses: the ledger's chain lock serializes it with the engines' sealers across processes (src/concordance/ledger.py:232-265), the CAS store is idempotent, a seal already chained is not chained again (src/concordance/receipts.py mint, FileExistsError), and a mark already kept is skipped. (4) READ BACK: every listed hash is in the CAS and verifies (cas.verify); each of the entry's sticks reads back by id with every sealed mark carrying its listed seal; the ledger's chain verifies after the mint (ledger.verify_chain). The result file records the run id, the name, the entry hash, each seal with new or present, the ledger's and the CAS's counts before and after, each stick id with its tick count before and after, the marks added, the memory reading and peak, and a status (minted, present, refused or failed), quoting only paths relative to data/. It exits non-zero on anything but minted or present. RETRACT: tools/stick_mint.py retract <name> runs the same lock, environment and step (1), then appends a retract event (src/concordance/tickstick.py:277) for each of the entry's sealed marks whose seal is listed, on each of its sticks, and reads back that each is gone and the ledger unchanged; it is idempotent. A cited mark or a note has no withdrawal in the keeping today, which is named as a want, so an entry's marks are reviewed as tracked source before they mint.

THE UNIT, tools/stick_mint.py mint|retract <name> --root <root> --run-id <id>, runs on the box under data/mints/.lock, a lock held only by mints that the kernel drops if the process dies (a second mint is refused and writes its refusal only to its own run id's result). It refuses to start unless available memory is at least its cap plus 256 MB, records the reading, and runs itself at oom_score_adj 1000 under nice and ionice, so if memory runs short the kernel ends the mint, never an engine; the step sets the cap from the measured peak (checker-102 measured about 73 MB per canary mint, line 3), at most 1024 MB, as the address-space limit where the platform supports it, and the test shows a mint completes under it there. It never begins the mint (step 3) more than 10 minutes after it started, refusing instead, so it finishes inside the 15-minute poll. Its environment holds no CONCORDANCE_ variable from its parent and is exactly the one the listed hashes come from: CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR=<root>/data, CONCORDANCE_SEAL_INDEX=0 (tools/tick.py's cold seal path: the CAS object, the ledger link and the receipt card are written, the live corpus is not touched, src/concordance/receipts.py:55-64), CONCORDANCE_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_S=1800, CONCORDANCE_RIEMANN_MAX=1e9, WEB_FIND_DISABLED=1, and src/ of <root> on its import path. It refuses if <root>/.env names any keeping location (CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR, CONCORDANCE_CAS_DIR, CONCORDANCE_LEDGER_DIR, CONCORDANCE_SEAL_INDEX, CONCORDANCE_PUBLIC_BASE), reading the names only, and unless the engine's installed unit, read as systemctl show nh-engine --property=Environment, names CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR=<root>/data, so it mints into the keeping the engine reads; a test gives systemctl as a stand-in. Every ledger.verify_chain the unit reads is taken while it holds the ledger's own chain lock (src/concordance/ledger.py:231-269), so no engine sealer writes mid-read; checker-102 measured the lock held about 1.5 s per read on a ledger of the box's size (line 6), twice per mint, and the result records how long each hold took. It never restarts an engine: GET /sticks and GET /stick fold data/sticks.jsonl on each request and answer no-store (line 3), and the receipt cards join at the next corpus load, as they always have for tick.py.

THE ORDER, fail-closed, writing nothing under data/ but data/mints/ before step 3. (1) Load the catalog from <root>/data/sticks with concordance.sticks.load_catalog and take the entry; refuse unless it is a data entry whose file hashes to the listed hash; read ledger.verify_chain and refuse unless it is ok. (2) REHEARSAL: in a scratch keeping outside data/ that holds only a copy of <root>/data/sticks.jsonl, and in a child process of its own, started with the unit's environment except that CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR names the scratch keeping, so that no module state it leaves (cas._COLD_CARDS_WRITTEN, cas._COLD_SPINE_WRITTEN, science_cards._MINTED and any other) can reach the mint, run concordance.sticks.run(entry) exactly as step 3 will, so tick's own refusals (the kind, the claim and source lengths, the seal, a bound that does not pass the stick's current bound, src/concordance/tickstick.py:237-275) apply to every mark against the box's current sticks; refuse unless run returns 0, the scratch CAS holds exactly the listed hashes, and every mark of the entry reads back on its stick in the scratch keeping by the mint_marks predicate (src/concordance/sticks.py mint_marks: kind, claim, seal, source, up_to, unit), cited marks and notes included. Then WOULD ADD, read only from the real keeping, names every write step 3 can make: for each listed hash, its CAS object; its ledger record, found by the ledger's own naming (the file ledger.seal_to_ledger writes for the precedent id receipts.mint gives it, ledger://<axis>/<first 16 hex>, through ledger._slugify, which turns an underscore into a hyphen, src/concordance/ledger.py:272-283 and :339), and checked by its record_hash; its receipt card (data/receipt_cards.jsonl, id cas.receipt_card_id) only when the CAS object is not yet there, since the cold path writes a card only when it creates the object (src/concordance/cas.py:78-82), an object already present without its card being recorded in the result as such and never required; and its verified card where the rehearsal wrote one and the object is not yet there (data/verified_cards.jsonl; none for a numeric seal, whose trail has no claim); each of the entry's sticks; and each mark the rehearsal added beyond the copy. If nothing would be added, the status is present and step 3 is never run, so a present mint leaves every file under data/ byte-identical except data/mints/; a line marked expect=present refuses if anything would be added. (3) MINT: concordance.sticks.run(entry) on the real keeping, the same seal path and mint loop tools/tick.py uses: the ledger's chain lock serializes it with the engines' sealers across processes, the CAS store is idempotent, a seal already chained is not chained again (src/concordance/receipts.py mint, FileExistsError), and a mark already kept is skipped. (4) READ BACK: for each listed hash, the CAS object verifies (cas.verify) and its ledger record is there by the ledger's own naming with that record_hash; for each CAS object this mint created, its receipt card is there (and its verified card where the rehearsal wrote one); every mark of the entry reads back on its stick by the mint_marks predicate; the marks added equal the rehearsal's exactly; ledger.verify_chain is ok. Anything missing makes the status failed, naming each missing item, with exit non-zero; since receipts.py:150-160 swallows a failed ledger append, a mint whose CAS write held and whose chain write failed reads failed here, and a later --mint of the same name completes it (the CAS object present, the ledger record chained then), which a test shows. The result file records the run id, the name, the entry hash, each item of WOULD ADD and of the read back, each stick id with its tick count before and after, the marks added, the memory reading and peak, the step it ended at, and a status (minted, present, refused or failed), quoting only paths relative to data/. The ledger's and the CAS's totals before and after are recorded for information only: the status rests on the per-hash readings, never on a count, since a seal from the site's own traffic moves the totals. It exits non-zero on anything but minted or present.

It reads back that each withdrawn mark is gone and, per hash, that no listed hash's CAS object or ledger record changed, never by a total, since the site's traffic moves the totals. What stays served after a retract: the stick, with its cited marks and notes, and every CAS object, ledger record and receipt card, which /s/<hash> and /seals (its total checksum) keep serving. A cited mark or a note has no withdrawal in the keeping today, which is named as a want, so an entry's marks are reviewed as tracked source before they mint.
